title: Relative colimits in a fiber tested by all local transports
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, colimits and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], relative colimit diagrams and right join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $q:E\to S$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories such that its pullback along each edge $a:\Delta^1\to S$ is a cocartesian fibration. For a vertex $s$ put $E_s=E\times_S\{s\}$. For an edge $a:s\to t$, a transport functor for $a$ is a functor $a_!:E_s\to E_t$ for which there is a simplicial map $H:E_s\times\Delta^1\to E\times_{S,a}\Delta^1$ over $\Delta^1$ with $H|_{E_s\times\{0\}}$ the inclusion, $H|_{E_s\times\{1\}}=a_!$, and every edge $H|_{\{x\}\times\Delta^1}$ cocartesian for the edge pullback. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $c:K^{\triangleright}\to E_s$ any diagram. For a diagram $u:K^{\triangleright}\to E_t$ with cone vertex $v$, its induced coherent cocone $u|_K\to\Delta_Ku(v)$ is the precomposition of $u$ with the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ that sends a simplex $(\sigma,\alpha)$, $\alpha:[n]\to[1]$, to the join simplex whose initial block is $\sigma$ restricted to $\alpha^{-1}(0)$ and whose final block is $\alpha^{-1}(1)$ at the cone vertex. Then the composite $K^{\triangleright}\xrightarrow{c}E_s\hookrightarrow E$ is a $q$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every edge $a:s\to t$ of $S$ and every transport functor $a_!$ for $a$, the induced coherent cocone of $a_!c$ is colimiting in $E_t$. Degenerate edges are included. No other colimits are assumed; neither global cocartesian lifts nor coherence of transports under composition is assumed. All objects lie in a fixed sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 4.3.1.10 and its proof, printed pp. 265-266 (PDF pp. 283-284). Read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks Project tag states this quasicategorical criterion. WANTED: archived HTT in literature/.

proof.text: Write $p=q$, $\mathcal E=E$, $\mathcal B=S$, and $b=s$ for the data of the statement. Put $a=c|_K$, $x=c(*)$, and let $\alpha:a\to\Delta_Kx$ be the induced coherent cocone. Every strict fiber is a quasicategory: an inner-horn problem in the fiber lifts against $p$ over the constant base simplex. Fix an edge $f:b\to b'$ and put $\mathcal E_f=\mathcal E\times_{\mathcal B,f}\Delta^1$, with projection $p_f$. By hypothesis $p_f$ is a cocartesian fibration. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p_f$, so its horn-cocartesian edges satisfy the mapping-space hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. All uses of that transport theorem below are for $p_f$, over $\Delta^1$. Transport functors exist: apply its diagram-lifting assertion to the inclusion $\mathcal E_b\to\mathcal E_f$ over the constant $0$ diagram and the constant transformation $0\to1$, in a containing universe. The resulting endpoint lies in $\mathcal E_{b'}$ and its lifting cylinder is a witness of the kind required in the statement. For any specified transport functor $f_!$ and its witness $H$, set $c_f=f_!c$ and $\lambda=H\circ(c\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1})$. The componentwise assertion of the same theorem, for shape $K^{\triangleright}$, makes $\lambda:c\to c_f$ cocartesian over the constant $0\to1$ transformation for $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},p_f)$. Its boundary $\lambda_a$ and apex $\lambda_x$ are likewise cocartesian for $\operatorname{Fun}(K,p_f)$ and $p_f$. Write $a_f,x_f,\alpha_f$ for the boundary, apex and coherent cocone of $c_f$. These are restrictions of this one cylinder; no global cocartesian property of $p$ is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, proof: first pull back along the chosen edge, then choose a cocartesian transformation of the entire cocone.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the apex square is a homotopy pullback. Write $s=pz$ and abbreviate its four corners by
$$U_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z),\quad V_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(a,\Delta_Kz),\quad S_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,s),\quad W_z=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks).$$
The top map sends $u$ to $\Delta_K(u)\alpha$. Since $c$ lies in a strict fiber, $p\alpha$ is the identity coherent transformation of $\Delta_Kb$, so the bottom map is exactly $\delta:S_z\to W_z$, $f\mapsto\Delta_K f$. All these are spaces and the square includes its specified coherent commutativity, as required by that node.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reduction to outgoing-arrow tests; Kerodon 7.1.6.19 (02X1), colimit dual and apex formulation.

proof.text:
Here is the space calculation for that square. Form its path pullback $P_z=V_z\times^h_{W_z}S_z$ with projection to $S_z$, using the path model of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. The square is a homotopy pullback exactly when its comparison $\Phi_z:U_z\to P_z$ is a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], $P_z$ is a Kan complex, and its projection to $S_z$ is a map of Kan complexes. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to $\Phi_z$ over the identity of the Kan complex $S_z$. It is an equivalence exactly when its map on homotopy fibers is one for every vertex $f\in S_z$. The homotopy fiber of $P_z\to S_z$ over $f$ is naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_K f}(V_z\to W_z)$: in path data a point is $(v,h,\gamma,\lambda)$, where $\gamma$ joins the image of $v$ to $\delta h$ and $\lambda$ joins $h$ to $f$. Compose $\gamma$ with $\delta\lambda$ to obtain the single path to $\delta f$; conversely take $h=f$ and constant $\lambda$. Allowing an intermediate endpoint and its path is the contractible path-space factor, so these maps are inverse up to the endpoint-preserving path homotopies, with all higher data. Consequently the condition is precisely that
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{f}(U_z\to S_z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_K f}(V_z\to W_z)$$
is a weak equivalence for every edge $f:b\to s$. Empty $S_z$ is covered by the same fiber-detection theorem; no surjectivity or Kan-fibration assumption on either vertical map is needed.

source.place: Mapping-space reconstruction of the fiber test in the proof of Proposition 4.3.1.10.

proof.text:
Fix $z\in\mathcal E_s$ and $f:b\to s$, and let $\mathcal E_f$ and $p_f$ be as in step 1. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber] to the inner fibration $p$ and the edge $f$, once with shape $\Delta^0$ and the vertices $x\in\mathcal E_b$, $z\in\mathcal E_s$, and once with shape $K$ and the diagrams $a$ and $\Delta_Kz$. It makes $U_z\to S_z$ and $V_z\to W_z$ Kan fibrations, and through their constant-path inclusions it identifies their homotopy fibers over $f$ and over $\Delta_Kf$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_f}((x,0),(z,1))$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_f)}((a,0),(\Delta_Kz,1))$. By the naturality clause of that node, these identifications carry the fiber map of step 3 to $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$ formed in $\mathcal E_f$: $\delta$ is the constant-diagram map on the base, and $\alpha$ is an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_b)$ over the degenerate edge at $\Delta_K0$.

Now apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $p_f$ and the chosen lifts $\lambda_x,\lambda_a$ of step 1. In its object and $K$-diagram homotopy-fiber formulas, the base mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(0,1)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)}(\Delta_K0,\Delta_K1)$ have one simplex in each degree, by the same node, so the homotopy fibers are the whole mapping spaces. Its target strict fibers are $\mathcal E_s$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)$. So precomposition with $\lambda_x$ and with $\lambda_a$ gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_s}(x_f,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_f}(x,z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)}(a_f,\Delta_Kz)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_f)}(a,\Delta_Kz)$. Under them, the map of the previous paragraph corresponds to
$$\beta_{f,z}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E_s}(x_f,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)}(a_f,\Delta_Kz),\qquad v\longmapsto\Delta_K(v)\alpha_f.$$
Indeed, the single cylinder $\lambda$ has the coherent naturality square $\alpha_f\lambda_a\simeq\Delta_K(\lambda_x)\alpha$, the restriction of $\lambda:K^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E_f$ along $K\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1$. Hence precomposing $v$ with $\lambda_x$ and then with $\alpha$ agrees, up to that specified coherent homotopy, with first forming $\Delta_K(v)\alpha_f$ and then precomposing with $\lambda_a$. The resulting square of spaces commutes up to specified homotopy and its vertical maps are equivalences. So the fiber map of step 3 is a weak equivalence if and only if $\beta_{f,z}$ is. This holds for every specified transport witness $H$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, reduction to the edge pullback and comparison after a cocartesian transformation; the ambient-to-local mapping-space comparison is expanded using the existing inner mapping-fibration and path-comparison nodes.

proof.text: Assume first that every $f_!c$ is colimiting. For any $z\in\mathcal E$ and any $f:b\to pz$, apply the cocone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in the quasicategory $\mathcal E_{pz}$. It makes $\beta_{f,z}$ a weak equivalence, since $c_f$ is the specified transported colimit cocone. Steps 3-4 then make the apex square for this $z$ a homotopy pullback. This holds for all $z$, so step 2 proves that $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1.10, implication from all transported colimits to a relative colimit.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $c$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. Steps 2-4 show that $\beta_{f,z}$ is a weak equivalence whenever $f:b\to pz$. Fix $b'$ and an edge $f:b\to b'$, and let $z$ vary over every object of $\mathcal E_{b'}$. These are exactly the maps $\beta_{f,z}$ required by the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so $c_f=f_!c$ is a colimit in that fiber. The quantifier includes the degenerate edge at $b$. For $K=\varnothing$, $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_s)$ is the one-point category, so the very same criterion says each $x_f$ is initial; for $K=\Delta^0$ it says the transported cocone edge is an equivalence. Neither direction has assumed any colimit besides the particular $c_f$, nor weak contractibility of $K$.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Six steps prove the local fiber relative-colimit criterion. Transport is used only in each cocartesian edge pullback. The ambient mapping-space maps are Kan fibrations by inner exponentiation; their strict fibers are mapping spaces in that edge pullback, and path comparison identifies them with the needed homotopy fibers. The compatible transport cylinder then identifies the comparison with the ordinary cocone criterion. Zero new nodes and zero Mathlib leaves. Maintainer reader (2026-10-17): the inline comparison in step 4 (inner exponentiation, Kan fibration of ambient mapping-space maps, and the identification of their fibers over an edge with mapping spaces in the edge pullback) became the statement-only node lem-coef-infinity-edge-pullback-mapping-fiber, which step 4 now cites; the transport and naturality argument stays in the step.
